title: fix(cli): keep init and agents from breaking files, and apply every --where in logs

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+---
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+`evlog agents` and `evlog init` no longer delete or duplicate text in an `AGENTS.md` whose evlog markers are not one clean pair. A file that lost `<!-- evlog:end -->` got a second block on one run and lost the section below it on the next. Both commands now stop with `cli.AGENTS_MARKERS_UNPAIRED`, exit 1 and leave the file as it is. A marker quoted in a sentence or a code fence is read as text.
+
+`evlog init` also changes in four places:
+
+- A Nitro config that imports something else from `evlog/nitro` or `evlog/nitro/v3` gets `import evlog` along with `modules: [evlog()]`. It got the module entry with no import.
+- The seeded `errors.ts` and `audit.ts` parse when a service or a route starts with a digit (`_3dShopErrors`, `_2FA_PASSWORD_CREATED`) or a route holds a wildcard.
+- A failed `npx skills add` exits 1, and the `AGENTS.md` block no longer points at the skill that was not installed. `evlog agents` already did both.
+- A file that cannot be written stops the run with `cli.WRITE_FAILED`, which names the file and the ones written before it, under `--json` too. `evlog agents` does the same. Both printed a stack trace and left stdout empty.

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+---
+'@evlog/cli': patch
+---
+
+`evlog logs` applies every `--where` when the flag is repeated. Only the last clause applied, so `--where path=/a --where n=5` returned events on any path. An empty `--where`, which is what an unset shell variable expands to, is now a usage error with exit 2.
+
+An event whose `duration`, `level` or `service` is not text no longer crashes every view, `--json` included.
+
+A `--where` value is a number only when it spells one exactly. `zip=123` no longer matches `"00123"`, a 19-digit id no longer matches its neighbours, and `amount>5000` no longer matches a field that holds text such as `"n/a"`. Write the value as the field holds it: `zip=00123`.

@@ -66,3 +66,22 @@ export function checkFlags(rawArgs: readonly string[], args: ArgsDef, bare: read
 
   return checked
 }
+
+/**
+ * Every value given to a flag that may repeat, in the order written. citty
+ * keeps the last one only.
+ *
+ * Call it on arguments {@link checkFlags} accepted: the flag is then followed
+ * by its value or carries it after `=`.
+ */
+export function flagValues(rawArgs: readonly string[], name: string): string[] {
+  const flag = `--${name}`
+  const end = rawArgs.indexOf('--')
+  const values: string[] = []
+  for (let index = 0; index < (end === -1 ? rawArgs.length : end); index++) {
+    const arg = rawArgs[index]!
+    if (arg === flag) values.push(rawArgs[++index]!)
+    else if (arg.startsWith(`${flag}=`)) values.push(arg.slice(flag.length + 1))
+  }
+  return values
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
+import { dirname } from 'node:path'
+import { cliErrors } from '../errors'
+import type { FileAction } from './wiring'
+
+/**
+ * Write the planned files in order.
+ *
+ * @throws `cli.WRITE_FAILED` at the first file that cannot be written, naming
+ * it and the files written before it. The files after it are not attempted.
+ */
+export async function writeActions(actions: readonly FileAction[]): Promise<void> {
+  const written: string[] = []
+  for (const action of actions) {
+    try {
+      await mkdir(dirname(action.path), { recursive: true })
+      await writeFile(action.path, action.contents, 'utf8')
+    } catch (error) {
+      throw cliErrors.WRITE_FAILED({
+        file: action.relative,
+        reason: (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? (error as Error).message,
+        written,
+        cause: error as Error,
+      })
+    }
+    written.push(action.relative)
+  }
+}
